title: JavaScript functions, closures, and object lookup
outcome: Predict captured values, call-time this, and property lookup in everyday UI code.
useCase: Event handlers, timers, reusable utilities, and callback APIs.
drawbacks: Retained state and implicit receivers can hide ownership.
version: Modern JavaScript / TypeScript · Vue 3.5 where applicable · browser APIs

trace.title: Create function
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

A function can keep access to variables from the scope where it was created. That is a closure.

It captures a binding, not always a frozen copy of the value. A later mutation can change what a callback reads.

Each function call can also create a separate binding, which is why a factory can give each widget private state.

For a normal function, this depends on how it is called. obj.method() supplies obj. Taking const fn=obj.method and calling fn() loses that receiver in strict mode.

An arrow keeps this from its enclosing scope; it does not acquire a new receiver through obj.arrow().

Objects have their own properties and a prototype chain. A missing own property can still be found on the prototype.

Use Object.hasOwn when ownership matters. Prefer Map for arbitrary key/value lookup when object-prototype behavior would be surprising.

These rules explain callbacks and objects; you rarely need to build a custom inheritance tree for a Vue page.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Trace creation → retained binding → callback invocation. Distinguish the value at registration from the value at execution.

Then trace the call expression to find this.

For object lookup, check own properties first, then the prototype chain. Object.create(null) has no usual Object prototype; it also lacks methods such as hasOwnProperty.

Object.hasOwn(obj,key) works without calling a method from untrusted input.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
A callback can keep large objects alive after the screen closes. A detached method can lose this.

Checking obj[key] alone can confuse absent values with inherited properties or valid falsey values.
